result.answer: For every real x with x≠2, (x²−4)/(x−2)=x+2. The original expression has domain ℝ\{2}. Although x+2 is defined at x=2, the original quotient is not; therefore the simplified expression is not equivalent to the original at every real number.

approaches.description: Factor the numerator and cancel the common factor only after restricting to the original domain.
approaches.reason: It establishes the simplification while retaining the excluded input.

change_log: Retained the valid factor-and-cancel argument, with explicit expansion of the factorization.
Made the cancellation restriction and the exceptional value x=2 explicit.
Removed the unnecessary dependency of the non-equivalence conclusion on the simplification claim; the domain fact and direct evaluation suffice.
No audit objection remains unresolved: the supplied checks support factorization, domain, restricted cancellation, and failure of global equivalence.

claims.basis_reference: Derived in domain-step from the denominator condition.
Derived in cancel-step using factorization and the nonzero denominator condition.
claims.statement: For every real x in ℝ\{2}, (x²−4)/(x−2)=x+2.

claims.basis_reference: Derived in non-equivalence-step by comparing both expressions at x=2.
claims.statement: x+2 is not equivalent to (x²−4)/(x−2) at every real number.

proof_steps.justification: The numerator is defined for every real x, while x−2=0 exactly when x=2; a quotient requires a nonzero denominator.
proof_steps.statement: The original quotient is defined exactly when x≠2.

proof_steps.justification: When x≠2, x−2 is nonzero, so ((x−2)(x+2))/(x−2)=x+2.
proof_steps.statement: On ℝ\{2}, the quotient simplifies to x+2.

proof_steps.justification: At x=2, x+2=4 is defined, whereas the original quotient is undefined because its denominator is zero.
proof_steps.statement: The original and simplified expressions do not agree in value-status at every real x.
